concepts.label: Assessment date
concepts.definition: Date when the EPC/APE assessment or diagnostic visit was carried out.
concepts.comparability_note: Administrative semantics vary slightly by country, but all mapped fields refer to the date of assessment/inspection/visit rather than validity end.

sources.qualifier: certificate issue/assessment date merged in source
sources.note: Could reflect issuance rather than visit date.

concepts.notes: Barcelona data_entrada appears more like entry/registration date and is left out.

concepts.label: Certificate registration date
concepts.definition: Date when the certificate was lodged, registered, received, or established in the administrative system.
concepts.comparability_note: Different systems use establishment, reception, lodgement, or registration dates; these are administratively related and often close in time but not always identical.
concepts.notes: Administrative date fields are common but not perfectly equivalent.

concepts.label: Certificate valid until
concepts.definition: Date until which the certificate remains valid.
concepts.comparability_note: Validity periods are policy-defined and comparable as dates, though the underlying legal duration differs by country and period.

concepts.label: Construction year
concepts.definition: Reported year of original building construction.
concepts.comparability_note: Some sources record exact year, others may contain placeholders, implausible values, or year of main construction only. Renovation is not consistently reflected.
concepts.notes: London and Lisbon expose construction period/age band rather than exact year.

concepts.label: Construction period
concepts.definition: Reported construction age band or period category for the building.
concepts.comparability_note: Period boundaries are country-specific and policy-specific; categories should not be compared as identical bins without recoding.

sources.qualifier: regulatory era rather than pure construction period
regulatory era rather than pure construction period

concepts.label: Building or dwelling type
concepts.definition: Reported typology of the certified residential asset, such as apartment, house, flat, fraction, or whole building.
concepts.comparability_note: Cities mix dwelling-level and building-level typologies, and category systems differ substantially. Comparison requires harmonizing apartment/house/building distinctions.

sources.note: Mostly residential dwelling type in building context.

concepts.notes: Amsterdam Gebouwsubtype and London built_form are related but more specific form descriptors.

concepts.label: Certificate context or status
concepts.definition: Administrative context of the certificate such as existing building, new building, final, provisional, or project/completed state.
concepts.comparability_note: Administrative status labels vary strongly across national registries and should not be treated as a common rating outcome.

concepts.label: Certification method or software
concepts.definition: Methodology, calculation engine, or software used to produce the certificate.
concepts.comparability_note: This concept is itself about methodology; it is useful for stratification and crosswalks, not for substantive comparison.

concepts.label: Postal code
concepts.definition: Postal code for the certified property address.
concepts.comparability_note: Postal code formats differ by country but the concept is straightforward.
concepts.notes: Other cities provide municipality/district but not clear postal code fields in the digest.

concepts.label: Street name
concepts.definition: Street name component of the property address.
concepts.comparability_note: Address normalization varies but the concept is standard.

concepts.label: House number
concepts.definition: Primary house or street number of the property address.
concepts.comparability_note: Some systems split house number and suffixes; only the main number is captured here.
concepts.notes: Amsterdam Huisletter and Huisnummertoevoeging are related address suffixes and left unmatched.

concepts.label: Municipality or commune
concepts.definition: Municipality, commune, or city name/code associated with the property.
concepts.comparability_note: Administrative levels differ, but all mapped fields identify the municipality/local authority area around the property.
concepts.notes: Liège city field includes sub-municipal variants/postcodes; not mapped here.

concepts.label: Climate zone
concepts.definition: Climate zone classification used in the EPC methodology.
concepts.comparability_note: Climate zone taxonomies differ by country and season; values are not directly comparable without country-specific decoding.

concepts.label: Longitude
concepts.definition: Longitude coordinate of the property location in geographic CRS.
concepts.comparability_note: Comparable when provided in geographic coordinates only.
concepts.notes: Core location concept present in only one city within this digest.

concepts.label: Latitude
concepts.definition: Latitude coordinate of the property location in geographic CRS.
concepts.comparability_note: Comparable when provided in geographic coordinates only.
concepts.notes: Core location concept present in only one city within this digest.

concepts.label: Projected X coordinate
concepts.definition: Projected planar X/easting coordinate of the property location.
concepts.comparability_note: Projected CRS differs across countries and sources; numeric values are not directly comparable without CRS metadata.

concepts.label: Projected Y coordinate
concepts.definition: Projected planar Y/northing coordinate of the property location.
concepts.comparability_note: Projected CRS differs across countries and sources; numeric values are not directly comparable without CRS metadata.

concepts.label: Floor area
concepts.definition: Reported area of the certified asset, usually dwelling/building usable, habitable, heated, thermal-zone, or cadastral area.
concepts.comparability_note: Area definitions differ materially across registries: thermal-zone area, habitable area, ground floor area, total floor area, cadastral area, and heated floor area are not equivalent. They are grouped here only because they share unit and represent the main size measure of the certified asset.

sources.qualifier: ground floor area label used as main size field

At building certificate level rather than dwelling.

concepts.label: Number of storeys
concepts.definition: Reported number of storeys or levels for the dwelling/building.
concepts.comparability_note: Some sources refer to building storeys, others to flat storeys or dwelling levels; values are related but not identical.

concepts.label: Floor-to-ceiling or floor height
concepts.definition: Reported interior height or representative floor height for the certified asset.
concepts.comparability_note: Paris reports ceiling height, while London and Dublin report floor heights that may represent different geometric constructs.

concepts.label: Wall area
concepts.definition: Reported total area of walls in the envelope or geometry model.
concepts.comparability_note: Envelope segmentation and whether areas are exposed, all walls, or modeled wall types differ by methodology.

concepts.label: Roof area
concepts.definition: Reported total area of roof elements in the envelope or geometry model.
concepts.comparability_note: May represent exposed roof only, predominant roof type, or aggregated modeled roof elements.

concepts.label: Floor element area
concepts.definition: Reported area of floor elements in the building envelope or geometry model.
concepts.comparability_note: Can refer to exposed floors, intermediate floors, or specific floor elements rather than total internal floor area.

sources.note: Distinct from total dwelling floor area in this schema.

concepts.label: Window or glazed area
concepts.definition: Reported total glazed/window area in the envelope or geometry model.
concepts.comparability_note: Sources may include windows only or all glazed openings; exposed-area conventions differ.

concepts.label: Door area
concepts.definition: Reported total door area in the envelope or geometry model.

concepts.label: Wall U-value
concepts.definition: Thermal transmittance of wall elements.
concepts.comparability_note: Sources may report representative, modeled, or type-specific wall U-values. Aggregation conventions differ.

concepts.label: Roof U-value
concepts.definition: Thermal transmittance of roof elements.

concepts.label: Floor U-value

concepts.label: Door U-value
concepts.definition: Thermal transmittance of doors.

concepts.notes: Core EPC concept present in one city only.

concepts.label: Building compactness
concepts.definition: Compactness indicator reported by the EPC model, typically reflecting form factor such as envelope-to-volume relation.
concepts.comparability_note: Definition is methodology-specific and not clearly identical across countries, but both mapped fields appear to represent the same modeling construct.

concepts.label: Energy performance class
concepts.definition: Ordinal energy label/class assigned by the national EPC methodology.
concepts.comparability_note: Energy class scales and thresholds differ by country and over time. Some countries use A-G, others use sub-classes like A2/C1, and the underlying metric varies.
concepts.notes: Potential ratings are excluded from the canonical current-state concept.

concepts.label: CO2 emissions class
concepts.definition: Ordinal class/label assigned to greenhouse gas emissions performance.
concepts.comparability_note: CO2 class scales are country-specific and can reflect different scopes and thresholds.

concepts.label: Energy efficiency score or index
concepts.definition: Numeric score/index used by the national EPC system to summarize energy efficiency or rating position.
concepts.comparability_note: These numeric scores are highly country-specific: Dutch EnergieIndex, Irish BER kWh/m2-equivalent score, UK SAP-derived efficiency score, and similar constructs are not directly comparable.
concepts.notes: Potential scores are left unmatched rather than merged with current-state score.

concepts.label: Primary energy intensity
concepts.definition: Primary energy use per unit floor area, as reported by the certificate methodology.
concepts.comparability_note: Primary energy scope differs across countries: total primary, fossil primary, or non-renewable primary. These are related but not equivalent; source qualifier must be respected.

sources.qualifier: fossil primary energy intensity, forfaitary variant

sources.note: Commonly an intensity-like indicator, but exact scope differs.

concepts.notes: A cross-city comparable intensity concept is essential, but qualifier differences are substantive.

concepts.label: Primary energy total
concepts.definition: Total primary energy consumption of the certified asset over a year.
concepts.comparability_note: Scope differs by country and by end-use coverage. Some fields are non-renewable primary only or specific subsets of end uses.
concepts.notes: No clean all-end-use total is available in Dublin except some less-complete TotalDeliveredEnergy-like fields for delivered, not primary.

concepts.label: Final energy intensity
concepts.definition: Final energy use per unit floor area, as reported by the certificate methodology.
concepts.comparability_note: End-use coverage differs; some sources cover 5 uses, others broader/narrower scopes. Still, final energy intensity is often more interpretable than totals.
concepts.notes: Madrid final_* fields appear likely intensities but unit evidence is weak, so not forced.

concepts.label: Final energy total
concepts.definition: Total final energy consumption of the certified asset over a year.
concepts.comparability_note: Coverage varies by end uses and treatment of renewable/self-generation. Dublin fields are end-use totals; Paris provides 5-use total.

sources.qualifier: delivered energy total rather than final energy total

concepts.label: Delivered energy total
concepts.definition: Total delivered energy to the asset over a year.
concepts.comparability_note: Delivered energy is distinct from final or primary energy and may exclude/export on-site generation depending on methodology.

unmatched.reason: Several cities report potential/future ratings or parallel subsystem classes, but semantics vary and they are not consistently present enough to define a clean cross-city current-state concept pair.
Heating, cooling, ACS/DHW, and lighting class labels recur, but category meaning depends on local methodology and subsystem definitions; unification would produce many low-coverage concepts.

Both cities contain wall/roof/floor/window quality descriptions or efficiency grades, but one is free-text/ordinal component assessment and the other is modeled insulation quality; not confidently equivalent.

unmatched.theme: heating and cooling demand limit/reference thresholds
unmatched.reason: Threshold/limit fields such as Eis* and cal_*limite are regulatory reference values rather than measured/certified property outcomes, and definitions differ too much.
Biomass, geothermal, district network, CHP, wind turbine, and broader ENR categories recur, but each appears in different structure and specificity, preventing conservative unification.
Dublin has permeability test results and leakage proxies, Paris has air-renewal losses, and London has corridor/ventilation context; related theme but not the same measurable quantity.

unmatched.theme: address subcomponents like apartment unit, staircase, floor level
unmatched.reason: Fields such as escala, pis, porta, floor_level, numero_etage_appartement, huisletter, and house-number suffixes recur but represent heterogeneous addressing conventions and vertical position, not a single stable concept.
Fields for certificate holder, geocoding provenance, UPRN source, or RNB provenance are administrative metadata with no robust common underlying quantity.
BAG IDs, SA codes, commune codes, UPRN-related provenance, and similar identifiers recur, but they are jurisdiction-specific identifiers rather than a unified cross-city concept.

unmatched.theme: thermal comfort and summer overheating indicators
unmatched.reason: Temperatuuroverschrijding and indicateur_confort_ete are related to summer comfort/overheating but use different scales and constructs.
Lisbon provides façade glazing areas by orientation, while Paris has crossing-dwelling and solar protection indicators; not enough direct overlap for a unified concept.
These datasets expose rich multi-generator, multi-installation hierarchies, but field structures are too source-specific to canonically align conservatively without inventing a complex nested schema.

summary: The draft vocabulary captures the strongest recurring EPC concepts across the eight cities: dates, construction period/year, asset type, floor area, climate zone, major energy and emissions indicators, ratings, and core building systems. The main caveats are methodological: area definitions differ sharply, rating classes and numeric scores are country-specific, and energy/emissions metrics vary in scope between primary/final/delivered and total versus intensity forms.
